name: mendezmendez — The Present
tagline: 891 daily digital collages by Chema Mendez, one per day since January 2024
description: The Present is the daily-art archive on Chema Mendez's (mendezmendez) own portfolio site: one new digital collage every day since January 2024, presented as a single dense chronological grid. Each piece merges public-domain paintings and illustrations, photography, 3D renders, AI-generated imagery, and the artist's own sketches into surreal, conceptual compositions with blunt one- or two-word titles ("Pixel Poisoning", "Corruption Engine", "Brain Fog", "Feed Poisoning"). The site also carries his other series — Entropy, First Impressions, Vanitas, Signature Series, Singularity, Alien Intelligence, Principia, CUBIQUE, Robert Mallary Portraits, Azar, and 2009-2020 — plus About, Shows and Contact. It is a visual-reference archive, not a downloadable asset library.
agent_guidance: Treat this as an art-direction mood source, never as an asset source — every image is the artist's copyrighted work and the page is a plain Squarespace image grid with no API, no alt-text semantics beyond the title, and no download rights. Reach for it when a brief asks for surreal digital-collage, glitch, or techno-melancholy visual language and you need a coherent 891-piece corpus to point a human art director at, or to mine the title list for naming and copy tone. Do not scrape it into a generator or reproduce a piece; link to the work and credit Chema Mendez instead.
why_it_matters: It is one of the most sustained daily-practice archives in digital collage — nearly 900 consecutive pieces on one voice — which makes it far more useful as a style reference than any single hero image. The single-page chronological grid also happens to be a good study in how to present a very large body of visual work without pagination.
notable_for: digital collage of public-domain art plus 3D and AI
eleven parallel series on one site
evidence: https://www.mendezmendez.com/the-present (WebFetch + raw HTML parse; extracted 891 unique artwork titles from image alt attributes and the site's series navigation)

name: mendezmendez on X
tagline: Artist's X account — daily collage drops, work-in-progress, and release notices
description: The X (Twitter) account of Chema Mendez, who posts under the handle mendezmendez. It is the primary release channel for his daily art practice: each new piece from The Present and his animated series is posted here first, alongside process notes and drop announcements. Useful as a chronological feed of the work; it is not a catalogued archive.
agent_guidance: Do not try to fetch this with a plain HTTP client — x.com serves a JS shell to unauthenticated agents and blocks scrapers, so any content you 'read' from it is a hallucination risk. If you need the work itself, use mendezmendez.com/the-present, which is server-rendered and complete; come here only when the user explicitly wants the live feed or the artist's own commentary on a specific drop. Cite the handle, not scraped post text.
why_it_matters: It is the artist's live release channel, so it is the only place where a new piece appears the day it is made — worth keeping in the index as the canonical pointer even though it is unreadable to agents.
evidence: Not fetched by instruction (x.com); record built from the pre-supplied title, description and og_image for https://x.com/mendezmendez

name: A Conversation with mendezmendez
tagline: SuperRare interview on daily collage practice and the First Impressions animations
description: A SuperRare editorial interview with Chema Mendez (mendezmendez), published 6 August 2026 by An Rong (anloremi). It covers his 2024 shift from weeks-long perfectionist compositions to a daily practice, his sourcing from public-domain paintings, photography, 3D renders, AI imagery and his own sketches, and the making of First Impressions — his first animated collection, where "pointillist textures meet Muybridge's motion studies, forming loops that reimagine 19th-century experiments with light, color, and time." Named references include Seurat, Signac, Eadweard Muybridge, and Alexander Kanoldt's 1907 Morgensonne. It is the single best written source on how the work is actually made.
agent_guidance: Read this first when a user asks what mendezmendez's work is or how to describe it — it is the only source in this cluster with a first-person account of method, and it hands you the exact art-historical vocabulary (pointillism, Muybridge motion studies, Neo-Impressionism) to write an accurate brief instead of guessing from thumbnails. Pair it with mendezmendez.com/the-present for the visual corpus. Note the pieces discussed are minted NFTs, so any 'recreate this style' request needs an originality guardrail, not a copy.
why_it_matters: Process documentation is rarer than portfolios; this interview explains the daily-constraint method that produced 891 works, which is transferable craft knowledge even for people who will never make a collage.
notable_for: first-person account of a daily-art constraint
names the Muybridge and Neo-Impressionist sources
documents the First Impressions animated series

name: mendezmendez on SuperRare
tagline: Artist profile listing three minted collections totalling 131 works
description: The SuperRare marketplace profile for mendezmendez (wallet 0x2c3b...fab7a). It groups his minted output into three collections — First Impressions (20 animated works), The Present (100), and Principia by mendezmendez (11) — for a total of 131 pieces, each individually priced in ETH. The page is a Next.js client-rendered app: collection names and counts are in the initial HTML, but bios, prices and per-work detail only appear after hydration.
pricing_detail: Works listed individually in ETH; no price shown without JS hydration
agent_guidance: Use this only to establish provenance and the canonical collection split (First Impressions 20, The Present 100, Principia 11) — a headless fetch returns a half-hydrated shell, so never quote prices, follower counts or bio text you 'read' here without a real browser. For visual reference go to mendezmendez.com; for method go to the SuperRare editorial interview. Treat every work as a minted, owned asset: link, do not reproduce.
why_it_matters: It is the authoritative provenance record for which of the ~891 daily pieces were actually minted and sold, which is the difference between a sketch archive and a body of collected work.
notable_for: First Impressions animated series lives here

name: The Present on NINFA
tagline: Curated NINFA subdomain for The Present, chapter five: Terms & Conditions
description: A dedicated NINFA curated-collection microsite for mendezmendez's The Present, currently showing chapter five, "Terms & Conditions" — five works on "the ways technology, mortality, and human emotion intertwine in contemporary life" — alongside roughly 78 pieces from earlier chapters (Binge Scrolling, Blue Light Addict, Ego Death, Screen Life, Alone Together, Brain Fog and so on). The collection carries the artist's own statement on the daily-art challenge begun in January 2024 and an accompanying NINFA essay, "Being Human Today: A Chapter by Chema Mendez." Works are minted on Ethereum (contract 0x36dec883b1e52c49f3c80b471953a3d2a010cb18) and listed in ETH.
pricing_detail: Individual works listed in ETH; observed listings ranged roughly 1.64-3.29 ETH
agent_guidance: This is the best-curated presentation of The Present — chapter statements, an essay, and a coherent hang — so send a human here rather than to the raw 891-image grid when they want to understand the series rather than browse it. It is a Next.js app that renders nothing useful to a plain fetch; the readable content lives in the streamed flight payload, so use a real browser or parse `self.__next_f` if you must extract it programmatically. Prices and availability move, so never cache an ETH figure from it.
why_it_matters: It shows the daily archive edited into chapters with a written thesis, which is the step most prolific creators skip — a useful model for anyone turning a large body of work into something a viewer can enter.
notable_for: curated edit of a 900-piece daily series
accompanying NINFA essay on the artist
